title: Grammar: Concessive Structures — Acknowledging and Countering Arguments
grammarTip:
Структуры уступки (Concessive structures) в аргументированном тексте:

ПЕРЕД уступкой:
Although / Even though / Though + clause:
"Although the data is limited, the conclusions are valid."

While / Whilst + clause:
"While some argue for X, the evidence supports Y."

Десмотря на → Despite / In spite of + noun/-ing:
"Despite the difficulties, the project succeeded."
"In spite of being expensive, the solution is effective."

ПОСЛЕ уступки:
However / Nevertheless / Nonetheless / Yet:
"The data is limited. Nevertheless, the trend is clear."

💡 Формула сильного аргумента:
"Concede" → "But" → "Your stronger point"
"While X is true, Y is even more important because..."

grammarTable.subject: Concessive conjunctions (before clauses)
grammarTable.verb: although / even though / though / while / whereas
grammarTable.example: "Although consequentialism has great force, it can justify counterintuitive conclusions."

grammarTable.subject: Concessive adverbs (sentence start)
grammarTable.example: "The argument is compelling. Nevertheless, serious objections remain."

grammarTable.subject: Concessive phrases (formal)
grammarTable.verb: that said / be that as it may / granted that / admittedly
grammarTable.example: "Admittedly, Kant's theory has intuitive appeal. That said, its application can be rigid."

grammarTable.subject: Concessive conditionals
grammarTable.verb: even if / even when / no matter how/what
grammarTable.short: Even if X were true, Y still holds
grammarTable.example: "Even if the numbers favour the action, the means matter morally."

grammarTable.subject: Partial agreement
grammarTable.verb: to some extent / up to a point / in certain respects
grammarTable.example: "To some extent, consequences do matter. But they are not the only moral consideration."

grammarTable.subject: Formal concessive phrases
grammarTable.verb: notwithstanding / despite / in spite of + noun/gerund
grammarTable.example: "Notwithstanding these objections, care ethics makes a valuable contribution." / "Despite its limitations, the theory offers real insight."

grammarExtra.title: Concessive Conjunctions: although, even though, while, whereas

rows.form: although / even though + clause (= despite the fact that)
rows.example: "Although consequentialism is powerful, it cannot fully account for individual rights."

rows.form: "even though" = stronger emphasis on the contrast
rows.example: "Even though the action saved lives, it violated a fundamental right."

rows.form: "while" = softer, often used for contrasts of a similar kind
rows.example: "While deontology respects persons, consequentialism respects outcomes."

rows.form: "whereas" = sharper contrast, often between opposites
rows.example: "Consequentialism focuses on outcomes, whereas deontology focuses on duties."

grammarExtra.title: Concessive Adverbs: however, nevertheless, nonetheless, yet, still

rows.form: "however" = most common, introduces a contrast after a full stop or semicolon
rows.example: "Kant's system is logically rigorous. However, its conclusions can seem inflexible."

rows.form: "nevertheless / nonetheless" = more emphatic; "the point is acknowledged, but..."
rows.example: "The objections are serious. Nevertheless, the core insight remains valuable."

rows.form: "yet" = literary/formal; same meaning as "however" at the start of a sentence
rows.example: "The argument has force. Yet it fails to account for individual dignity."

rows.form: "still" = despite this, the situation remains the same
rows.example: "The theory has been criticised. Still, it is widely taught and defended."

grammarExtra.title: Formal Concessive Phrases: "that said," "be that as it may," "admittedly," "granted"

rows.form: "admittedly" = I acknowledge/concede this point
rows.example: "Admittedly, the theory cannot resolve every dilemma. That said, it offers a useful framework."

rows.form: "granted (that)" = granting the point for the sake of argument
rows.example: "Granted that consequences matter, it does not follow that they are all that matters."

rows.form: "be that as it may" = even if that is true (very formal)
rows.example: "Be that as it may, the counter-argument has not been adequately addressed."

rows.form: "that said" = having acknowledged the above
rows.example: "The objections have merit. That said, they do not undermine the main argument."

grammarExtra.title: Concessive Conditionals: "even if," "even when," "no matter how"

rows.form: "even if + clause" = whether or not this is true, the result stays the same
rows.example: "Even if torturing one person saved a thousand lives, it would remain morally impermissible."

rows.form: "even when" = in all cases when (generalising)
rows.example: "Even when consequences are good, the method may be wrong."

rows.form: "no matter how/what/where" = regardless of degree
rows.example: "No matter how beneficial the outcome, using a person as a mere means is wrong."

rows.form: Note: "even if" uses the same tense as normal conditionals
rows.example: "Even if this argument were correct (hypothetical), it would not justify the conclusion."

grammarExtra.title: Degree Concession: "to some extent," "up to a point," "in certain respects"

rows.form: "to some extent" = partially true but not completely
rows.example: "To some extent, consequences do matter morally. But they cannot be all that matters."

rows.form: "up to a point" = true within limits but not beyond them
rows.example: "The argument is persuasive up to a point — it breaks down in extreme cases."

rows.form: "in certain respects / in some ways"
rows.example: "In certain respects, care ethics complements rather than contradicts deontology."

rows.form: "it is true that X, but Y" = direct acknowledgement + counter
rows.example: "It is true that the argument has intuitive force. But intuition is not always a reliable guide."

exercises.text: "___ consequentialism has genuine strengths, it faces serious objections about rights."
exercises.hint: "Although + clause" = concession — even though X is true, Y is also the case

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct concessive adverb.
exercises.text: "The argument is compelling. ___, it has significant weaknesses." (= despite being compelling)
exercises.hint: Concessive adverb after a full stop

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct formal concessive phrase.
exercises.text: "___ the objections are serious, they do not undermine the overall argument."
exercises.hint: "Admittedly, X. [But Y]" = I acknowledge the objection

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct concessive conditional.
exercises.text: "___ the action produced good outcomes, using a person as a mere means would remain wrong."
exercises.hint: "Even if X were true, Y still holds"

exercises.text: "The objections have merit. ___ ___ ___ ___, the core insight of care ethics is sound."
exercises.hint: "Be that as it may" = even if the objections are valid, the main point stands

exercises.text: "___ some extent, virtue ethics captures something the other frameworks miss. But it too has limitations."
exercises.hint: "To some extent" = partially true but not completely

exercises.instruction: Choose the concessive connector that best shows sharp contrast.
exercises.text: "Consequentialism evaluates outcomes, ___ deontology evaluates the nature of the act itself."
exercises.hint: "Whereas" = sharp contrast between two opposing things within one sentence

exercises.text: "___ ___ consequences matter, it does not follow that consequences are all that matters."
exercises.hint: "Granted that X" = accepting X for the sake of argument before countering

exercises.text: "___ the argument has intuitive appeal, it is not supported by careful reasoning."
exercises.hint: "While X, Y" = even though X is the case, Y is also the case

exercises.text: "___ how beneficial the consequences are, the means still matter morally."
exercises.hint: "No matter how + adjective" = regardless of degree

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct structure for partial agreement.
exercises.text: "The argument is persuasive ___ ___ ___. It breaks down when taken to extremes."
exercises.hint: All three express partial agreement: "up to a point / to some extent / in some ways"

exercises.instruction: Complete with "it is true that... but..."
exercises.text: "___ the theory has limitations. ___, these limitations do not invalidate its core claim."
exercises.correct: It is true that / That said
exercises.hint: "It is true that X. That said/However, Y."

exercises.instruction: Which sentence uses a concessive structure correctly?
opts: "Although it is a good argument, but it has weaknesses."
"Even though the argument is strong, it faces objections."
exercises.correct: "Even though the argument is strong, it faces objections."
exercises.hint: "Even though + clause, Y" — correct; "although... but" = double conjunction error

exercises.text: "Despite the objections, care ethics makes a valuable contribution." → ___ these objections, care ethics makes a valuable contribution."

exercises.instruction: Which is the most formal concessive phrase?
exercises.hint: "Notwithstanding" is the most formal; "but" is the most informal

exercises.instruction: What error does this sentence contain?
exercises.text: "Although Kant's argument is powerful, but it can be inflexible."
opts: "Although... but" is incorrect — use one conjunction only
exercises.correct: "Although... but" is incorrect — use one conjunction only
exercises.hint: "Although X, Y" — do NOT add "but": "Although X, Y" OR "X, but Y" — not both

questions.text: "___ virtue ethics focuses on character, consequentialism focuses on outcomes." (sharp contrast)
questions.hint: "Whereas" = sharp contrast between two opposing things in one sentence

questions.text: "The theory is intellectually elegant. ___, it faces serious practical objections." (concessive adverb)
questions.hint: Concessive adverb at the start of the second sentence

questions.text: "___ the consequences would be beneficial, using a person as a mere means remains wrong."
questions.hint: "Even if + clause" = concessive conditional — whether or not X is true, Y still holds

questions.text: "___ ___, the objections to care ethics do not undermine its central insight." (formal: even if that is true)
questions.hint: "Be that as it may" = formal phrase: even if all that is true, the main point stands

questions.text: "Consequentialism has genuine strengths. ___, its critics raise important objections."
"Although the argument is compelling, but it has weaknesses" is grammatically correct.
questions.hint: "Although X, Y" OR "X, but Y" — never "although... but" together

questions.text: "___ ___ how compelling the evidence, philosophical questions about responsibility remain." (= regardless of degree)
questions.hint: "No matter how + adjective" = regardless of degree

questions.text: "___, consequences matter morally. But they are not the only consideration." (= I acknowledge this point)
"The argument is persuasive ___ ___ ___ — it becomes problematic in extreme cases." (= true within limits)
questions.hint: "Up to a point" = true within limits, not beyond them

questions.text: "___ these limitations, the ethics of care makes a genuinely important contribution." (formal — despite)
"___ ___ consequences matter, it does not follow that they are all that matters." (= granting the point)
questions.hint: "Granted that X" = accepting X for argument's sake, then countering

questions.text: Which uses a concessive structure correctly in academic writing?
opts: "Although the argument is powerful, but it has limitations."
questions.hint: "Even though + clause, result clause" = correct concessive structure
